deep.reconstruction:
Context (cote 154, 1983-84). Grothendieck is studying systems of pseudolines (pseudo-droites, PsDS) in the real projective plane. Around a given arrangement X he builds an auxiliary cellular space 𝔛 by gluing pieces along sides. 𝔛 behaves like a parameter or dual space of pseudolines 'swept' across X; the previous page speaks of 'rives de balayage' (sweep fronts), arcs of transitions and specialisations, and vertices (D_i, t, ω). 𝔛 comes with a map 𝔛 → X. He also wants a parallel transport on 𝔛 of combinatorial data (the 'structures' of faces) along paths. The previous page ends with the worry that it is unclear to what extent transport on PsDS is given by a local system on 𝔛.

The figure is a local model of a 'superposingular band'.
- Green lines are pseudolines of the configuration. Two near-horizontal green lines bound a band whose central line is drawn red-dashed.
- Vertical green lines are transverse lines. At each one there is a small arc labelled ν or ν' with a short blue tick, where orange curves cross.
- Orange curves are curves of 𝔛 (sweep curves / dual pseudolines). They pass through the band, pinching and crossing at points on the green lines and on the central line.
- The counts n−ν and n−1−(ν−1)−(ν'−1) record how many of the n lines lie on one side at the various positions.

The text compares two versions of the 'superposingular gluings'.
1. The drawn version keeps the band of finite width. It is adapted to studying the map 𝔛 → X, but not to the structures of the faces or to their parallel transport.
2. In the other version one flattens the band onto its central line (red dots). Crossing a superposingular position then induces a parallel transport that is not the identification of sides used to build 𝔛. It is the antipodal of that identification.

Hence, for a path on 𝔛, the transport τ_X on X and the 'transport-reflection' τ_𝔛 on 𝔛 satisfy τ_X = σ^ν τ_𝔛. Here σ is the antipodal involution and ν is the number of 'antipodisms', i.e. the number of crossings of superposingular lines.

In modern terms, the naive gluing local system on 𝔛 differs from the geometric one by a Z/2-valued cocycle. That cocycle is the mod-2 intersection number of the path with the superposingular locus, a codimension-1 wall. In other words the true transport is the gluing transport twisted by a Z/2 local system / double cover, much like the antipodal twist in the space of lines of RP² (a Möbius band). This answers in part the worry of the previous page: transport is a local system up to this explicit sign twist. The next page moves on to maps with even vertices and faces and chains of five commuting involutions.
errors: No mathematical error is visible on the page. The formula τ_X = σ^ν τ_𝔛 is consistent with σ being an involution, so only the parity of ν matters. The claim is stated without proof, and the precise definition of 'superposingular' is not on this page.

ideas.what: Two models of gluing near a 'superposingular' locus: a thick band versus a band flattened onto its central line. Each is suited to a different purpose (the map 𝔛 → X versus transport of face structures).
ideas.modern_name: Thickened versus collapsed wall models in a cell complex / blow-up versus contraction of a codimension-1 stratum

ideas.what: Parallel transport on 𝔛 differs from the side-identification transport by the antipodal map at each crossing of a superposingular line: τ_X = σ^ν τ_𝔛, with ν the number of crossings.
ideas.modern_name: Z/2 twisting of a local system by a wall-crossing cocycle (mod-2 intersection with a hypersurface), comparable to the orientation double cover / antipodal monodromy on the Möbius band of lines in RP²

ideas.what: Use of a sweep/dual space 𝔛 attached to a pseudoline arrangement X to study transport of combinatorial structures.
ideas.modern_name: Topological sweeps (Edelsbrunner–Guibas) / allowable sequences (Goodman–Pollack) / spaces of pseudolines relative to an arrangement
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck's pseudoline work is not, to my knowledge, published; it is possibly alluded to in Récoltes et Semailles (unsure).

missed.claim: Grothendieck's construction of a space 𝔛 attached to a pseudoline arrangement, with transport of face structures governed by a local system twisted by a Z/2 wall-crossing sign, appears to be an undeveloped program. It is not reflected in the pseudoline-arrangement literature.
missed.quote: τ_X = σ^ν τ_𝔛, où ν est le nombre d'antipodismes
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This could connect to monodromy questions on the realization spaces and sweep spaces of oriented matroids of rank 3. It is of modest interest unless the full construction of 𝔛 is reconstructed from the surrounding pages.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a technical working note: a choice between two gluing models and a sign-twist formula for transport. The formula is natural and routine once the setup is fixed. Its interest is mainly historical, as part of Grothendieck's little-known 1983-84 pseudoline work.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'Version des recollements superposingulières' (the word is 'superposingulier/ère', not 'superposi-gulations').
'on aplatit la bande superposingulière sur sa courbe centrale (pointillés rouge)' rather than 'sur la con[?] centrale'.

'mais est l'antipodique de celui-ci. Donc la relation entre transport parallèle τ_X sur X, et transport-réflexions τ_𝔛 sur 𝔛, pour un chemin donné sur 𝔛, est τ_X = σ^ν τ_𝔛' ('Donc', not 'Dans la'). The symbol in the formula looks like σ written over a struck letter.
'où ν est le nombre d'antipodismes, i.e. le nombre de franchissements d'une ligne superposingulière.'
The interlinear insertion reads '(de franchissement d'une position superposingulière)'.
The figure labels are ν (second vertical), ν' (third and fourth verticals), 'n−ν' on the upper green line, and 'n−1−(ν−1) −(ν'−1)' near the right vertical.
